text: The Indian government launched the National Health Mission (NHM) in 2013, with the aim of providing universal access to equitable, affordable, and quality health care services. The mission has two sub-missions: the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM). As of 2022, the NHM has achieved significant milestones, including a decline in infant mortality rate from 57 per 1000 live births in 2005-06 to 32 per 1000 live births in 2020-21. The mission has also led to an increase in institutional deliveries from 20% in 2005-06 to 89% in 2020-21. The government has allocated Rs 27,989.60 crore for the NHM in the 2022-23 budget, a 10% increase from the previous year.
title: National Health Mission Overview

text: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY), also known as the Ayushman Bharat scheme, was launched on September 23, 2018. The scheme provides health insurance coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year to over 100 million poor and vulnerable families. As of January 2022, more than 3.4 crore beneficiaries have been treated under the scheme, with a total of Rs 45,148 crore spent on treatments. The scheme has a network of over 24,000 empaneled hospitals across the country, including public and private hospitals. The government has allocated Rs 6,400 crore for the PMJAY in the 2022-23 budget.
title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana

text: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NPPCD) was launched in 2010 to prevent and control non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, and cancer. The program has a budget of Rs 1,023.30 crore for the 2022-23 financial year. As of 2022, the program has established 596 District NCD Cells and 3,444 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres (CHCs) level. The program has also trained over 1.2 lakh healthcare professionals in NCD management. The program aims to reduce the prevalence of NCD risk factors by 10% by 2025.
title: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases

text: The National AIDS Control Programme (NACP) was launched in 1992 to prevent and control the spread of HIV/AIDS in India. The program has achieved significant success, with a decline in new HIV infections from 1.7 lakh in 2000 to 87,580 in 2020. The program has also increased the number of people living with HIV (PLHIV) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) from 1.2 lakh in 2007 to 14.4 lakh in 2022. The government has allocated Rs 2,500 crore for the NACP in the 2022-23 budget. The program aims to reduce new HIV infections by 75% by 2025.
title: National AIDS Control Programme

text: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) was launched in 2003 to prevent and control vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and chikungunya. The program has achieved significant success, with a decline in malaria cases from 2.9 million in 2000 to 1.2 million in 2020. The program has also increased the use of insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) from 10% in 2000 to 60% in 2020. The government has allocated Rs 1,500 crore for the NVBDCP in the 2022-23 budget. The program aims to eliminate malaria by 2030.
title: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme

text: The Indian government has launched several initiatives to improve the health infrastructure in the country. The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) was launched in 2006 to establish new AIIMS-like institutions and upgrade existing government medical colleges. As of 2022, six new AIIMS have been established under the scheme. The government has also launched the Kayakalp Scheme in 2015 to improve the cleanliness and hygiene in public health facilities. The scheme has covered over 15,000 public health facilities across the country.
title: Health Infrastructure Development

text: The National Health Policy (NHP) 2017 was launched on March 15, 2017, to provide universal access to equitable, affordable, and quality health care services. The policy aims to increase the government's health expenditure to 2.5% of the GDP by 2025. The policy also aims to reduce the out-of-pocket expenditure on health care from 62% in 2015-16 to 30% by 2025. The policy has set several targets, including increasing the life expectancy at birth from 67.5 years in 2015-16 to 70 years by 2025.
title: National Health Policy 2017

text: The Indian government has launched the e-Health India initiative to promote the use of information and communication technology (ICT) in the health sector. The initiative aims to create a national health information network to facilitate the sharing of health data and information across the country. As of 2022, the initiative has established a national health portal, which provides information on various health schemes and programs. The initiative has also promoted the use of telemedicine services, with over 1.5 lakh telemedicine sessions conducted in 2020-21.
title: e-Health India Initiative

text: The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) was launched in 2010 to provide health care services to the elderly population in the country. The program has established 30 geriatric departments in medical colleges and has trained over 1,000 healthcare professionals in geriatric care. As of 2022, the program has covered over 100 districts across the country. The program aims to provide comprehensive health care services to the elderly population, including preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services.
title: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly

text: The Indian government has launched the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) in 2013 to provide health screening and treatment to children in the age group of 0-18 years. The program has screened over 10 crore children across the country as of 2022. The program has identified over 1.5 crore children with health defects, who are being provided with treatment and management. The program aims to reduce the infant mortality rate and the under-5 mortality rate by 2025. The government has allocated Rs 1,000 crore for the RBSK in the 2022-23 budget.
title: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram

text: The Indian government has been implementing various schemes to provide subsidies to farmers, with the aim of increasing agricultural productivity and income. As per the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare's annual report for 2020-21, the total outlay for agricultural subsidies was Rs. 1,34,399 crore. The report also suggested that the government should focus on providing subsidies to small and marginal farmers, who account for over 80% of the total farming community in India. As per the Agriculture Census 2015-16, there are over 12.6 crore farmers in India, out of which 10.3 crore are small and marginal farmers.
title: Recommendations on Agricultural Subsidies

The NCS portal is a part of the government's effort to improve employment outcomes and provide better job opportunities to the youth.
title: National Career Service Portal

text: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2020-21 report highlights the employment trends in India. The report states that the unemployment rate in the country has declined to 4.2% in 2020-21 from 5.1% in 2019-20. The survey also reveals that the labor force participation rate (LFPR) has increased to 40.1% in 2020-21 from 39.4% in 2019-20. The report further notes that the employment rate in the formal sector has increased to 22.1% in 2020-21 from 20.6% in 2019-20. The PLFS report is conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO) to provide a comprehensive picture of the labor market in India.
title: Periodic Labour Force Survey 2020-21

The scheme provides a subsidy to employers for new employees hired, with the government paying the employer's contribution to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) for a period of three years. As of March 2022, the scheme has benefited over 1.5 lakh establishments and has led to the creation of over 1 crore new jobs. The PMRPY scheme is a part of the government's effort to promote employment and reduce unemployment in the country.
title: Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana

text: The Ministry of Labour and Employment has notified the Code on Social Security, 2020, which provides for a comprehensive framework for social security in India. The code consolidates and amends nine existing labor laws, including the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948. The code provides for universal social security coverage, including pension, health insurance, and unemployment benefits, for all workers in the organized and unorganized sectors. The code also provides for the establishment of a National Social Security Board to oversee the implementation of the code.
title: Code on Social Security, 2020

As of January 2022, the scheme has trained over 1 crore youth, with over 70% of them being placed in jobs. The PMKVY scheme is a part of the government's effort to enhance the employability of the youth and promote skill development in the country.
title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana

title: National Clean Air Programme

title: Environmental and Social Management Framework
